definition: VoTT (Visual Object Tagging Tool) was a free and open source Electron app for image annotation and labeling developed by Microsoft.
details: The software is written in the TypeScript programming language and used for building end-to-end object detection models from image and videos assets for computer vision algorithms. The VoTT source code is licensed under MIT License and available on GitHub. As of December 7, 2021, the project was no longer being maintained and its GitHub repository was made read-only.

explainer.lead: VoTT (Visual Object Tagging Tool) was a free, open-source Electron app from Microsoft for annotating and labeling images. It mattered for building end-to-end object detection models from image and video assets.

tiers.eli5: It was a free tool for drawing boxes around objects in pictures so a computer could learn to find them.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers used it in TypeScript-based workflows to label image and video data for computer vision training; a pitfall is that the project stopped being maintained on December 7, 2021, and its GitHub repository became read-only.
tiers.paperLevel: It is an MIT-licensed Electron application written in TypeScript for image annotation and labeling, used to build end-to-end object detection models for computer vision. Its known limit is that it is no longer maintained.

explainer.example: A team labels bounding boxes on a video dataset in VoTT to train an object detector.
